extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: A benchmark for real-world travel planning with language agents. It provides a sandbox environment, tools for accessing millions of data records, and 1,225 curated planning intents and reference plans for evaluating whether agents can satisfy multiple constraints.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su
extraction.rai:dataCollection: TravelPlanner was constructed as a benchmark by creating a static and closed sandbox environment, randomly generating diverse travel queries from fundamental elements (departure city, destination, date range), and then having 20 graduate students meticulously annotate feasible reference plans. The authors also performed detailed review and quality control of every query and plan.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Missing or unavailable information in the sandbox was handled by agents dynamically seeking alternatives; the paper also notes that when cities lacked transportation or attractions, agents typically resorted to hallucination or omitted an answer, and environment constraints were reflected in the evaluation rather than separately assessed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: A static sandbox database with around four million data entries crawled from the Internet, accessed via six tools: CitySearch, FlightSearch, DistanceMatrix, RestaurantSearch, AttractionSearch, and AccommodationSearch.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The sandbox data is based on 2022, and the paper’s example queries/plans use dates in 2022; no explicit overall collection start/end dates are given.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: They invited 20 graduate students to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries; one plan was eligible only if it met all constraints in the evaluation script. The authors then performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying errors, and re-calibrated each query’s budget using costs from the human-annotated plans.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality was checked through detailed author review of every query and plan, with errors corrected; multiple stages of human verification were used to ensure high quality and at least one feasible solution.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least one human-annotated plan per query; the paper does not specify multiple independent annotations per item.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate natural language queries, and GPT-4-Turbo was used in the experiments to extract key components from plans.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Some of the data in the TravelPlanner environment is derived from publicly available data on the Internet, and the authors note that "everyone’s definition of commonsense may be different"; the evaluation criteria are based on the authors’ consensus.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark’s commonsense dimension is limited by the authors’ consensus-based evaluation criteria, and the paper warns against cheating in validation and test sets to preserve fairness and reliability. It also implies that additional discussion is needed for a more thorough evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper positions TravelPlanner as a benchmark to advance future research in complex planning, and says releasing evaluation scripts will foster innovation and aid the development of new methods.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for benchmarking complex planning research, with evaluation scripts released for use in evaluation; the authors encourage using evaluation feedback in the training set, such as reinforcement learning techniques, but prohibit cheating in validation and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The database is created as a "static and closed sandbox environment"; queries are constructed by randomly choosing fundamental elements and adjusting duration/hard constraints; budgets are recalibrated using costs from human-annotated plans; and plans are manually annotated and quality-checked.

name.evidence: we propose TravelPlanner, a new planning benchmark that focuses on travel planning

description.evidence: we propose TravelPlanner, a new planning benchmark that focuses on travel planning, a common real-world planning scenario. It provides a rich sandbox environment, various tools for accessing nearly four million data records, and 1,225 meticulously curated planning intents and reference plans.
